knowledge:
- key_parameters: im_thresh=Importance threshold used to filter correlation-based SLPs to reduce false positives (default robust value is 0.0016, but can be estimated per cancer type using est_im) ;; mutgene=Vector of mutated genes used in corr_slp during random permutations for threshold estimation ;; nperm=Number of permutations/runs for estimating the importance threshold ;; kappa_value=Cohen's kappa coefficient threshold used to filter consensus SLPs (e.g., >= 0.6) ;; padj=Adjusted p-value threshold used to filter consensus SLPs (e.g., <= 0.1)
- alternatives: None mentioned; the documentation notes that mslp is unsupervised, does not rely on curated training sets, and explicitly integrates genetic screen data unlike other approaches.
- when_to_use: Use this pipeline when you want to identify context-specific synthetic lethal partners for loss-of-function mutations by integrating patient multi-omics data (mutation, CNA, expression, z-scores) and cancer cell line genetic screen data (e.g., DepMap, Project Drive).
- pitfalls: Running corr_slp, comp_slp, cons_slp, and est_im sequentially can be slow; it is highly recommended to set up a parallel backend using the future package (e.g., plan(multisession)). Input mutation profiles must contain the mandatory columns "Tumor_Sample_Barcode", "Gene" (containing Ensembl gene IDs), and "Variant_Classification".

workflows.name: mslp_consensus_pipeline
workflows.intent: Predict consensus synthetic lethality partners (SLPs) by integrating patient genomic/transcriptomic data and cell line genetic screen data.
input: screen_hit (Cell line genetic screen hits data frame/table)
workflows.stages: 1. Preprocess patient multi-omics data using pp_tcga ;; 2. Call compensation-based SLPs using comp_slp ;; 3. Call correlation-based SLPs using corr_slp ;; 4. Estimate the importance threshold for correlation SLPs using est_im ;; 5. Merge compensation and correlation SLP results using merge_slp ;; 6. Identify screen-supported SLPs in cell lines using scr_slp ;; 7. Calculate consensus SLPs across cell lines using cons_slp
workflows.code:
res <- pp_tcga(P_mut, P_cna, P_expr, P_z)

plan(multisession, workers = 2)
res_comp <- comp_slp(example_z, example_comp_mut)
saveRDS(res_comp, file = "compSLP_res.rds")
plan(sequential)

plan(multisession, workers = 2)
res_corr <- corr_slp(example_expr, example_corr_mut)
saveRDS(res_corr, "corrSLP_res.rds")

im_thresh <- 0.0016
res_f     <- res_corr[im >= im_thresh]
plan(sequential)

plan(multisession, workers = 2)
mutgene    <- sample(intersect(example_corr_mut$mut_entrez, rownames(example_expr)), 5)
nperm      <- 3
res_random <- lapply(seq_len(nperm), function(x) corr_slp(example_expr, example_corr_mut, mutgene = mutgene))
im_res     <- est_im(res_random)
res_f_2    <- res_corr[im >= mean(im_res$roc_thresh)]
plan(sequential)

plan(multisession, workers = 2)
res_comp   <- readRDS("compSLP_res.rds")
res_corr   <- readRDS("corrSLP_res.rds")
merged_res <- merge_slp(res_comp, res_corr)

screen_1 <- merged_res[, .(slp_entrez, slp_symbol)] %>%
    unique %>%
    .[sample(nrow(.), round(.8 * nrow(.)))] %>%
    setnames(c(1, 2), c("screen_entrez", "screen_symbol")) %>%
    .[, cell_line := "cell_1"]

screen_2 <- merged_res[, .(slp_entrez, slp_symbol)] %>%
    unique %>%
    .[sample(nrow(.), round(.8 * nrow(.)))] %>%
    setnames(c(1, 2), c("screen_entrez", "screen_symbol")) %>%
    .[, cell_line := "cell_2"]

screen_hit <- rbind(screen_1, screen_2)

mut_1 <- merged_res[, .(mut_entrez)] %>%
    unique %>%
    .[sample(nrow(.), round(.8 * nrow(.)))] %>%
    .[, cell_line := "cell_1"]

mut_2 <- merged_res[, .(mut_entrez)] %>%
    unique %>%
    .[sample(nrow(.), round(.8 * nrow(.)))] %>%
    .[, cell_line := "cell_2"]

mut_info <- rbind(mut_1, mut_2)

scr_res <- lapply(c("cell_1", "cell_2"), scr_slp, screen_hit, mut_info, merged_res)
scr_res[lengths(scr_res) == 0] <- NULL
scr_res <- rbindlist(scr_res)

k_res   <- cons_slp(scr_res, merged_res)
k_res_f <- k_res[kappa_value >= 0.6 & padj <= 0.1]

plan(sequential)
